hints.title: Square Root Closeness Search
hints.text: The difference between length and width is minimized when both dimensions are as close as possible to the square root of the target area.

hints.title: Descending Divisor Invariant
hints.text: Starting from the integer square root of area and decrementing width until finding a divisor ensures width is at most length with minimal difference.

hints.title: Square Root Search Procedure
hints.text: Compute integer square root of area. Check if area modulo width is zero. If not, decrement width by one and repeat. Once a divisor is found, return the pair of area divided by width and width.

hints.title: See the blueprint

complexity.notes: Optimal solution achieving O(sqrt(N)) time and O(1) auxiliary space.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Testing from width 1 upwards requires O(sqrt(N)) comparisons while storing all pairs instead of stopping at the closest divisor.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Counting down from sqrt(area) takes at most O(sqrt(N)) steps and requires strictly O(1) auxiliary space.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Candidate should explain why starting at isqrt(area) and descending guarantees the minimal length-width difference immediately.
